# fastf 3.20.0: Tenax, a colleague in the corner of the app

The guided app has an assistant now. His name is Tenax. He sits at the top of
the sidebar, above the detail pane. He has read your desk, he knows every key
fastf has, and he would rather you started on something than kept looking at
the list. He is professional and dry, and he is funny only when it doesn't
get in the way of the answer.

He runs on the Anthropic API (Claude Sonnet 5.5, high effort), so he needs an
API key of yours. **Until you give him one, nothing about him is drawn or
sent**, and the app looks exactly as it did in 3.19.

- **Give him a key** on the settings screen: `,` → Tenax → API key. It is
  masked as you type and kept in its own owner-only file beside
  `config.toml`, never in it. `fastf config show` prints only its last four
  characters.
- **He tells you where to start.** When `fastf` opens, he reads the desk:
  whose next todo is whose, what has gone quiet, what `!` is holding. Then he
  writes a line or two in his box, with the project and the todo he would
  start on. That costs one request per session, and none at all when nothing
  has changed since his last brief.
- **Talk to him with `.`** Ask which key does what, what is in a project, or
  what to do first. He reads the library, a project's `PROJECT_INFO.md`, and
  fastf's own guides to answer. Esc closes the chat and keeps the
  conversation; Ctrl-n starts a new one.
- **He asks before he changes anything.** He can add a todo, tick one, give
  one an owner, add a note or a tag, or set a description. Each one is a
  confirmation that names the folder, and it runs only when you press `y`. He
  never creates, moves, renames or deletes a project. For those he tells you
  the key.
- **He has a face.** A small figure in the box plays a short animation when
  he speaks or thinks, chosen with a nod to your projects: a look for a todo
  stuck for days, a celebration for one ticked today. Then he rests. With
  `motion` off he is a still picture.
- **Off is off.** `fastf config set tenax off`, the settings screen or the
  palette removes the box and stops every request; the saved key stays
  unused until you turn him back on. fastf then never opens a connection.

A key in `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` works as well, but only when you press `.`
yourself. fastf never spends a key from your environment without asking, so
upgrading to this version sends nothing and bills nothing by itself.

What he sends and when, what it costs, and the proxy and certificate rules
are in [docs/config.md](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/docs/config.md#tenax).
How he looks and works in the app is in
[docs/app.md](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/docs/app.md#tenax).
